body.statement:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) be independent centered random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), let \(X=m^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^m x_j\), and let \(Y\) be the centered Gaussian vector with the same covariance.  If every coordinate of \(X\) has variance between fixed positive constants, then Theorem 2.2 bounds the Kolmogorov distance between \(\max_{\ell\le p}X_\ell\) and \(\max_{\ell\le p}Y_\ell\) by
\[
 C\left[m^{-1/8}(M_3^{3/4}\vee M_4^{1/2})\log^{7/8}(pm/\gamma)
 +m^{-1/2}\log^{3/2}(pm/\gamma)u(\gamma)+\gamma\right]
\]
for every \(\gamma\in(0,1)\), with \(M_3,M_4\) and \(u(\gamma)\) defined in that theorem; Corollary 2.1 records the corresponding vanishing approximation under its leading moment regimes.  No restriction is imposed on correlations among coordinates.

attestation.note: Verified directly against the Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.1 environments in the arXiv TeX source.

body.justification: This is the degenerate-covariance-safe Gaussian approximation used for the sign-expanded event score.
body.gap: The cited theorem is generic probability substrate; the adaptation to the event-by-cell coefficients is proved in this note.
body.consumer: It supplies the oracle Gaussian approximation term in thm:uniform-multiplier-band.
